compile.summary: FP16 engine built in 124.5s — 256 TRT layers, 31.1 MB.
compile.detail:
**yolo11s.onnx → yolo11s.fp16.plan**  ·  TensorRT 10.13.3.9

The engine is on disk and this is the file that gets deployed. Nothing has been run yet, so none of this is a speed measurement — the build time above is how long it took to CREATE, not how fast it goes.

**Asked for FP16, but the engine is mixed:** FP16 201 · FP32 55.

TensorRT falls back when a layer has no kernel at the precision you asked for. This is the usual reason a speed-up comes in smaller than expected — the layers that fell back are still running at the slower format.

**Layout conversion — 29% of layers**

73 of 256 layers do no maths. They only rearrange data so the next layer can read it.

Around 8% is normal at FP32. What this number is really for is comparing two builds of the SAME model: a jump after a precision change is the cost of extra shuffling, not a worse choice of kernel. At 29% a large share of this engine is moving data rather than computing — worth comparing against another precision before concluding the model is simply expensive.

**What the engine is made of**

| Kind | Count | What it does |
|---|---:|---|
| CaskConvolution | 85 | convolutions |
| Reformat | 73 | layout/precision conversion — overhead, not maths |
| NoOp | 49 | removed entirely |
| PointWiseV2 | 30 | elementwise maths, fused |
| kgen | 4 | — |
| Shuffle | 4 | reshapes and transposes |
| CaskPooling | 3 | — |
| Constant | 3 | — |
| gemm | 2 | — |
| Resize | 2 | resizing |
| CaskSoftMaxV2 | 1 | — |

These are TensorRT's own kernel families, after it merged what it could — which is why the count does not match the ONNX node count.
warnings: First build on this GPU, so every kernel had to be timed (124s). The timings are now cached; rebuilding this model after surgery or quantization will be far quicker.
